content: Ofloxacin is a medication used to treat bacterial eye infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for other types of eye infections. To use ofloxacin eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above the eye and place one drop into the pouch. After applying the drop, look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye. Do not rinse the dropper after use. If you are using other eye medications, such as drops or ointments, wait at least 5 minutes before applying the next medication. Use ofloxacin regularly as prescribed to achieve the best results. Continue using it for the full duration prescribed, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects of ofloxacin may include temporary stinging or burning of the eyes, blurred vision, eye discomfort, itching, redness, dryness, tearing, sensitivity to light, or a sensation of something in the eye. These effects are usually temporary. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new fungal eye infection. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. Before using ofloxacin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other quinolone antibiotics (such as ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as preservatives like benzalkonium chloride, which can cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred or unstable. Use caution when driving or operating machinery until your vision stabilizes. During pregnancy, ofloxacin should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor or pharmacist. If someone overdoses on this medication and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center. Store ofloxacin at room temperature. Discard the solution if it changes color, becomes cloudy, or develops particles. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
